history.heading: The Maravi
paragraphs: Malawi, a narrow landlocked country along Lake Malawi in southeastern Africa, takes its name from the Maravi kingdom, founded by Bantu-speaking people around the 15th century. In the 19th century the region was raided by Ngoni invaders and by slave traders linked to the Swahili coast.

history.heading: Nyasaland
paragraphs: The Scottish missionary and explorer David Livingstone reached Lake Malawi in 1859, and Scottish missions followed. Britain declared the British Central Africa Protectorate in 1891, renamed Nyasaland in 1907. John Chilembwe led an uprising against colonial abuses in 1915. In 1953 Nyasaland was joined with the Rhodesias in a federation, against strong local opposition.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Malawi became independent on 6 July 1964 under Hastings Kamuzu Banda, who ruled as "President for Life" in a repressive one-party state. A 1993 referendum restored multiparty democracy. In 2020 Malawi's courts annulled a flawed presidential election, a landmark for African democracy, and the re-run was won by the opposition. Former president Peter Mutharika won the 2025 election, defeating the incumbent.

culture.heading: The Warm Heart of Africa
paragraphs: Malawi is known as "the Warm Heart of Africa" for the friendliness of its people. Chichewa and English are the main languages; ethnic groups include the Chewa, Lomwe, Yao and Tumbuka. Most people are Christian, with a significant Muslim minority.

The Gule Wamkulu masked dances of the Chewa are recognised by UNESCO. Nsima, a thick maize porridge, is the staple, and chambo fish from Lake Malawi is a delicacy. Lake Malawi has more species of fish than any other lake.

politics.heading: Presidential republic
paragraphs: Malawi is a presidential republic with a president elected for five years and a National Assembly. It has had several peaceful transfers of power, and its courts have shown independence. Corruption and economic management are central political issues.

economy.heading: Agriculture
paragraphs: Malawi is one of the poorest countries in the world. Most people are smallholder farmers. Tobacco is the main export, along with tea, sugar and soybeans.
Frequent droughts, floods and cyclones cause food shortages. Foreign currency shortages, high inflation and debt have strained the economy. The currency is the kwacha.
